case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court held that the Adoption Assistance and Child Welfare Act's requirement that states make reasonable efforts to prevent removal and reunify families creates no right enforceable by private individuals under section 1983 or directly under the Act.
key_cases.relevance: It locates enforcement of federal child welfare funding conditions with the Secretary rather than private plaintiffs.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the Act does not create an enforceable right on behalf of respondents.

key_cases.case_name: Floyd County Grand Jury v. Department of Family & Children Services
key_cases.holding: The Court of Appeals affirmed an order quashing grand jury subpoenas to seven DFACS employees, holding that county departments of family and children services are instrumentalities of the state Department of Human Resources rather than county offices, so a grand jury has no power under OCGA 15-12-71(b)(2) or any other statute to conduct a civil investigation of DFACS.
key_cases.relevance: It establishes that DFACS is a state instrumentality funded through state and federal channels, which locates financial audit authority at the state and federal level rather than with the county.
key_cases.quote: these departments are instrumentalities of the Department of Human Resources (DHR), a state agency, independent of the county, and no evidence has been presented to the contrary

key_cases.case_name: Perdue v. Kenny A. ex rel. Winn
key_cases.court: Supreme Court of the United States
key_cases.holding: The Supreme Court reversed the Eleventh Circuit in the Georgia foster-care class action, holding that a lodestar fee under 42 U.S.C. 1988 may be enhanced for superior attorney performance only in rare and exceptional circumstances supported by specific evidence, and that the district court's 75 percent enhancement was not properly justified.
key_cases.relevance: It sets the federal standard for scrutinizing the public cost of structural child-welfare litigation against a state agency, and is mandatory subsequent history for anyone citing the Eleventh Circuit's Kenny A. fee decision.
key_cases.quote: In the present case, the District Court did not provide proper justification for the large enhancement that it awarded.
